answer: Influence over a ballot is quadratically damped by how many identities share one history, so splitting a reputation R across n clones leaves each holding R over n and the group commanding R squared over n instead of R. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. Under this rule the sparrow of shared credit, the vault that separates one voice from many, and the bridge that carries a reputation are the three moving parts: none of them can be duplicated without shrinking the total.
